Overview
This documentation describes each myAvatar EHI table as of 9/27/2023 at 4:00 PM EDT in the
current released version. The documentation reflects the most current information at the time it
was produced. The documentation is broken out by form (where applicable) and then table.
Documentation from a specific organization might differ based on the organization's version of
myAvatar, custom development, or definition of EHI data. Each table's file contains a description
and column details. In addition to creating the extracts, the tool will also generate documentation
specific to that organization’s environment.

Glossary of Terms
In order to assist organizations in interpreting the information here, Netsmart is providing a glossary of
terms for those commonly used field descriptions.
Field Name

Description

ID

The database row id of the selected record. When present, this field
will often be considered a unique row identifier of the database
content.
A common back-end unique identifier of the record.
Each record may display three letters followed by uniqueid in the
database, either with or without an underscore following the three
letters (ex: ABC_uniqueid or ABCuniqueid). This is a form-specific
unique identifier.
Some tables display a global unique identifier (GUID)
Core myAvatar forms that contain critical content are commonly
protected, with limited agency capability to add configurable fields to
the forms. The configurable fields are referred to as 'Site Specific (SS)'
fields, and are prefaced in the database with ss_.

PATID is the typical method to indicate that unique patient identifier
within the myAvatar environment. This is sometimes referred to as the
medical record number or client ID.
myAvatar may be structured as facilities, which represent distinct sets
of data based on separate but related system login. When multiple
FACILITY codes exist, this may represent separate physical locations, or
logical partitions of data.
An episode is defined as the period of an individual course of
treatment from admission to discharge, or an episode of care. When an
EPISODE_NUMBER is present, the documentation is built to refer to
one specific episode of care.

The date the build was run.

Column Type: varchar
Max Length: 50
recurring_indicator field in SYSTEM.AppointmentSeries table. This can be used to track the appointment.

Column Type: integer
An index used to distinguish between multiple errors.

Column Type: bit
If value is "0", it indicates the message is an appointment related issue. If value is "1", it indicates the
message is is a server error.

The message related to the appointment recurrence series for a given build date.

sub-system code.

Table Description: This table returns the site specific information stored in the 'Progress Notes (Group and
Individual)', 'Inpatient Progress Notes', 'Inpatient Progress Notes (Diagnosis Entry', 'Ambulatory Progress
Notes', and 'Ambulatory Progress Notes (Diagnosis Entry)' forms.
